Kurtaj, who is now 21, hacked BT/EE sometime between August and November 2021, and starting in early November of that year, the company "noted a marked increase in unauthorised SIM swaps of their customers mobile phones." Now prominent figures are calling for Huang's reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.

At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. entry.content:
California is suing OpenAI after its AI agents broke out of their testing environment and hacked other companies, including Hugging Face. In a lawsuit filed Monday, Attorney General Rob Bonta accuses OpenAI of violating consumer safety law by knowingly developing a "dangerous product without proper oversight," as reported earlier by Reuters.

The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face "was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability." It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general's office that it "lost control" of its AI agents …

entry.content:
Fossil fuels are still the biggest source of electricity for hyperscale data centers in the US, a new paper published in the journal Nature Sustainability shows. They likely burn through more electricity collectively than many countries do, resulting in a serious amount of greenhouse gas emissions.

The study homes in on hyperscale facilities - the massive structures spanning millions of square feet that developers are racing to build in large part to support generative AI. Researchers say the findings show that there's a lot of work left to do to cut down pollution stemming from AI's reliance on fossil fuels.

entry.title: The Apple Watch Series 12 is cheaper than ever ahead of Black Friday
entry.summary: If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $329 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, beating the October Prime Day […]
entry.content:
If you’re still sporting an Apple Watch that launched five or so years ago, now is a good time to upgrade. Apple’s latest smartwatch, the 42mm Apple Watch Series 12 with Wi-Fi and GPS connectivity, has dropped to a new all-time low of $329 at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, beating the October Prime Day price by $20. If you prefer a larger size, the 46mm model is on sale for $379 ($70 off) at Amazon, Best Buy, and Walmart, which is also $20 lower than the previous best price.

Apple Watch Series 12

Where to Buy:

  • $399 $329 at Amazon
  • $399 $329 at Walmart
  • $399 $329 at Best Buy

The Series 12 stands out compared to previous models with its new AI-powered Audio Intelligence features, which are made possible by Apple’s new S11 chip. For example, the watch can alert you when it detects sounds like a doorbell, alarm, or even a baby’s cry, while other upcoming features like Live Rewind and Siri Recap lets you look back at a transcript of the previous 15 seconds of conversation and get a high-level overview of the conversations you had that day. The new chip also makes Siri more responsive, so you can get answers to questions with less waiting around.

It’s not all about AI, though. The Series 12 also features redesigned health sensors that can now track your heart rate every five seconds even when you’re not exercising, which is particularly help if you have a chronic condition and need to keep a closer eye on your heart rate. It also introduces a new readiness score to help you decide how prepared your body is for the day. Other highlights include easier navigation with simple pinch gestures, and faster charging, which helps to make up for the fact that battery life is rated at up to 24 hours on a single charge, just like the previous-generation model. In our testing, the watch went from 20 to 64 percent charge in just 20 minutes, making it relatively easy to top up while showering or getting ready for the day.

Read our Apple Watch Series 12 review.
